skills.description: How to turn a storefront question into get_context search targets, including the shop vocabulary that does not appear anywhere in the model. Replaces the built-in phrase-detection guide for this package.

skills.name: storefront-conventions
skills.description: What storefront's measures actually count, and the four places a reasonable reading of them is wrong. Read before answering any revenue, order, margin, or region question against this package.

payload.skills_note: This package ships its own guidance, listed above. Read the relevant one before relying on names or conventions from this package. If it is already loaded as a skill, use that; otherwise fetch it with get_skill(skill_name, scopes), and if that tool is not available to you, proceed and say which guidance you could not read. A guide whose name matches a built-in one replaces it here.

prompt: What the caller is looking for:
[1] overview - "The overview report's tiles, each over the order lines its controls select"
[2] order_items - "Order line items — the fact table, one row per product sold on an order"
[3] scoped_orders - "Order lines narrowed by the data app's control row. Every tile queries this."
[4] customers - "People who have placed orders — one row per customer, keyed by `customer_id`"
[5] products - "Catalog of products, one row per product, with cost and retail price"
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
Source: overview - The overview report's tiles, each over the order lines its controls select.
Its doc: "The overview report's tiles, each over the order lines its controls select"
[1] margin_rate (measure, number): Gross margin as a share of revenue
[3] total_margin (measure, number): Total gross margin (revenue minus cost of goods sold), summed per line
[4] percent_of_sales (measure, number): Share of total sales
[9] orders_per_customer (measure, number): Average orders placed per customer
[10] return_rate (measure, number): Share of line items that were returned
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

{"picks": [{"target": <target number>, "candidates": [<candidate numbers, best first>], "best": <the one candidate number that best answers the target>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}, ...], "caveats": ["<one short sentence>", ...]}

Give one element per target, with an empty "candidates" list for a target this source cannot answer. Use only the candidate numbers listed under that target. List "candidates" best first; "best" is one of them.
